title: MOFA thanks allies, like-minded countries, and friends in the international community for supporting Taiwan’s UN bid
text:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) sincerely thanks its allies, like-minded countries, and friends in the international community for voicing firm support of Taiwan’s participation in the United Nations (UN) system through various means at the General Debate of the 81st session of the UNGA and on its sidelines, as well as for refuting China’s distortion of UN General Assembly (UNGA) Resolution 2758. This helped set the record straight and increase the UN community’s understanding of and attention to Taiwan’s persistent and inappropriate exclusion.

During the General Debate, which concluded on September 28, senior government officials from diplomatic allies— including Palau, the Marshall Islands, Tuvalu, Eswatini, Belize, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Saint Christopher and Nevis, Saint Lucia, Paraguay, and Guatemala—extended support in various ways, such as speaking up for Taiwan at the General Debate and submitting letters.

The permanent representatives to the UN of Palau, the Marshall Islands, Belize, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, and Saint Lucia visited the UN Secretariat together to deliver a joint letter signed by Taiwan’s allies. Such concrete actions conveyed to UN senior officials these countries’ staunch support for Taiwan’s inclusion.

As for like-minded countries and the European Union, Czech Republic President Petr Pavel emphasized the importance of peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait at the General Debate. That marked the third time that he had raised the issue at the General Debate, following his previous statements in 2023 and 2025.

Following meetings on the UNGA sidelines, similar joint statements were issued by the foreign ministers of the United States, Japan, and the Republic of Korea, as well as the foreign ministers and senior officials of Australia, France, Germany, Japan, New Zealand, Poland, the Republic of Korea, and the United Kingdom. The documents stressed the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait and opposed all attempts to unilaterally change the status quo. The Chinese-language spokesperson for the US Department of State also reaffirmed US support for Taiwan’s meaningful participation in international organizations.

Moreover, the European Union pointed out that UNGA Resolution 2758 consisted of only 150 words and made no mention of Taiwan. It emphasized that Taiwan should be allowed to participate in international organizations, provided that Taiwan complied with their rules and practices. It also reiterated that peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait were of strategic importance to regional and global security and prosperity.

Additionally, the US House of Representatives, 15 US state legislatures, the Czech Republic Senate, the Polish Parliament, the Italian Parliament, the Brazilian National Congress, the Colombian Congress, and the European Parliament strongly backed Taiwan’s inclusion in the UN system and other multilateral organizations and mechanisms this year. They did so by passing resolutions, motions, and reports; issuing joint statements; and submitting letters in support of Taiwan.

AI is of great interest to the UN community, as well as a strong point of Taiwan. The government seeks to increase Taiwan’s visibility and influence in the field and help Taiwanese businesses explore opportunities through public-private partnerships. To this end, the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office in New York and the US-Taiwan Business Council (USTBC) jointly hosted the conference titled “AI For Good: Challenges and Opportunities for Taiwan” during this year’s UNGA.

At the event, Deputy Minister of Digital Affairs Isabel Hou delivered a keynote address and held a discussion with President of the USTBC Rupert Hammond-Chambers. Deputy Minister Hou stated that Taiwan was a global powerhouse in advanced chip manufacturing and a major producer of AI servers. She explained that despite these advantages, Taiwan was unable to participate in the UN system because of the distortion of UNGA Resolution 2758. This represented a great loss for the development of AI worldwide and the establishment of trustworthy AI supply chains.

A roundtable for AI enterprises was also held at the conference. Acer Medical General Manager Hsu Kai-cheng, Chunghwa Telecom Laboratories Assistant Manager Chou I-fan, and 11 related businesses based in New York attended the event. They exchanged views extensively on AI development and applications, as well as future directions of cooperation. The event marked another successful example of economic diplomacy.

This year, as of October 5, a total of 372 reports friendly to Taiwan had appeared in mainstream media outlets in 47 countries that featured an op-ed by Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung, articles by Taiwan’s overseas missions, or press interviews with heads of missions. These outlets included The New York Sun and Newsmax in the United States, The Hill Times in Canada, The Sankei Shimbun in Japan, The Jerusalem Post in Israel, City AM in the United Kingdom, the Philippine Daily Inquirer in the Philippines, El Economista in Mexico, La Nación in Argentina, Gazeta Wyborcza in Poland, and The Guardian in Nigeria. While promoting Taiwan’s bid during the UNGA, MOFA and its overseas missions made 1,432 posts on such social media platforms as Facebook, X, Instagram, and Threads, accumulating over 3.985 million views.

Meanwhile, MOFA thanks the cross-party delegation consisting of three members of the Legislative Yuan—Wang Yi-chuan, Yeh Yuan-chih, and Tsai Chun-chou—for traveling to New York to take part in related activities during the UNGA. This demonstrated to the international community that the Taiwan government’s campaign to participate in the UN system enjoyed strong backing from across the political spectrum and the public in Taiwan.

MOFA also rented billboard space at Times Square, at bus stops and newsstands, and on more than 1,000 New York City taxis; hired mobile LED billboard trucks; and organized other promotional activities to display the slogans “Taiwan—Powering AI, Connecting the World” and “Deliver for All: Chip in with Taiwan,” which echoed the theme of this year’s UNGA. These displays promoted Taiwan as an indispensable, critical force in global semiconductor manufacturing and AI development.

MOFA reiterates that following the end of World War II, the San Francisco Peace Treaty, which has the force of international law, superseded such political statements as the Cairo Declaration and the Potsdam Proclamation. The treaty did not hand Taiwan over to the People’s Republic of China (PRC). In reality, the PRC has never ruled Taiwan. Therefore, Taiwan is by no means part of the PRC.

In the mid-1980s, Taiwan started to undergo comprehensive liberalization and democratization, completing its first direct presidential election in 1996. By then, all central executive and legislative representatives of the ROC (Taiwan) government were being elected by the people of Taiwan, making it the sole legitimate government to govern and externally represent Taiwan. This also established the objective fact that the ROC (Taiwan) and the PRC exist on an equal footing, with neither being subordinate to the other.

UNGA Resolution 2758 made no mention of Taiwan. In addition, it neither determined that Taiwan was part of the PRC nor authorized the PRC to represent Taiwan in the UN system. Thus, it cannot serve as a basis for precluding Taiwan’s participation in the UN system or other international and multilateral mechanisms. Only Taiwan’s democratically elected government can represent the 23 million people of Taiwan in the UN system and other international organizations.

MOFA once again underscores the fact that China’s misrepresentation of UNGA Resolution 2758 aims to establish a legal basis for a possible future armed invasion of Taiwan. This is in grave violation of the principles enshrined in Article 2 of the UN Charter, which calls for the peaceful settlement of disputes and prohibits the use of threats and force in international relations.

MOFA solemnly urges the international community to jointly counter China’s malicious ambitions and calls on the United Nations to stop yielding to pressure from China. Instead, it should include Taiwan so as to achieve its goals of leaving no one behind and being a UN that delivers for all. (E)
